newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebel saboteurs hit key Colombian oil pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Rebel saboteurs hit key Colombian oil pipeline.

text.p: Suspected leftist rebels attacked a key oil pipline in northern Colombia for the 35th time this year, forcing the suspension of pumping operations and spilling thousands of barrels of crude, authorities said on Friday.

A spokesman for the state oil company Ecopetrol said the latest attack on the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline occurred on Thursday night in Norte de Santander province, near Colombia's border with Venezuela.

He said at least 8,000 barrels of crude oil had been spilled in the dynamite attack and that most of it had poured into a river system that empties into the Gulf of Venezuela off the neighboring country's Caribbean coast.
Venezuelan authorities were alerted of probable ecological damage from the attack which was carried out by suspected National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels, the spokesman said.
He added that repair work on the pipeline had been hampered by guerrilla activity in the area where it was dynamited, and said it was not immediately clear when pumping would resume.

The pipeline -- which was attacked 46 times in 1995 and has been dynamited 423 times since since 1986 -- carries 220,000 barrels of oil per day from the Cano Limon fields operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp. to the Caribbean port of Covenas.

The Ecopetrol spokesman said ELN guerrillas were also believed responsible for blowing up a natural gas pipeline on Friday in northern Magdalena province, in a rural area between the towns of Aracataca and Fundacion.

The pipeline, which carries gas into the interior from off-shore platforms operated by Texaco, could not be repaired immediately because of rebel landmines scattered around the area where it was ruptured, the spokesman said.

The ELN, Colombia's second largest guerrilla group, was founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966. It specializes in kidnappings and a nationwide campaign of economic sabotage targeting oil and coal facilities.
